from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
out=Path('tmp/pdfs')
out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (out/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
    print(f'PAGE {i+1}: {len(t)} characters')
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+(out/f'page-{i+1:02d}.txt').read_text() for i in range(len(r.pages))))
PY"

strengths: The method addresses a valuable computer-vision problem: scalable dataset distillation. Combining pretrained feature targets with class-specific BatchNorm matching provides a straightforward pipeline demonstrated on ImageNet-1K.

Table I reports consistent improvements over the reproduced SRe2L baseline. At 100 images per class, accuracy improves from 58.3% to 60.7% on ImageNet-1K and from 59.8% to 61.0% on Tiny ImageNet. These are useful empirical gains.

Reporting both published and reproduced SRe2L results, and explaining the training modifications, strengthens the comparison. Three-run evaluations, component ablations, regularization sensitivity, and cross-architecture experiments provide several perspectives on performance.

The manuscript clearly acknowledges its dependence on SRe2L, DeepInversion, existing barycenter algorithms, and the POT library. Pseudocode and supplementary recovery hyperparameters help communicate the overall method.
weaknesses: The central contribution needs clearer mathematical positioning. Equation (4) approximates one empirical distribution using a limited number of support points. With squared Euclidean feature distances and unrestricted learned masses, the stated unregularized objective is equivalent to k-means quantization. This connection is neither discussed nor experimentally controlled. Comparisons against k-means feature targets and MMD within the same teacher, regularization, and relabeling pipeline are needed to establish the claimed Wasserstein-specific advantage.

The ablation supports class-specific BatchNorm more strongly than the headline metric contribution. In Table III, adding barycenter matching while retaining cross-entropy and per-class BatchNorm changes accuracy by -0.1, +0.8, and +0.5 percentage points on ImageNette, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K, respectively. Most improvement over the reproduced baseline is already obtained through per-class BatchNorm. The integration remains useful, but the evidence does not convincingly establish the proposed metric as the main source of improvement.

Important formulation and implementation details remain unresolved. Equation (3) and Algorithms 2–3 optimize atom masses, but their use in the returned synthetic training dataset is not explained; matching support locations alone does not preserve the optimized distribution. Section III-B also describes entropic regularization, whereas the appendix presents unregularized transport programs without specifying an entropy coefficient. Barycenter initialization and concrete convergence settings are missing, limiting reproducibility.

The efficiency claim lacks a controlled measurement. Table IV reports only this method's per-image, per-update cost at 64×64 resolution, without a baseline or a breakdown of feature extraction and barycenter computation. The supplementary 14-hour ImageNet experiment is helpful, but does not establish comparative efficiency or the overhead introduced by the proposed method.

The broader experimental claims exceed the available controls. Table I does not clearly establish comparable image resolutions, architectures, and relabeling protocols for imported baseline results. Table II demonstrates some transfer, but lacks a corresponding SRe2L transfer baseline; ImageNet ViT-Tiny accuracy is only 7.5% at 10 images per class. These results support a narrower claim than general architectural adaptability.
